paper.title: A Denoising Pre-training Framework for Accelerating Novel Material Discovery
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces an unsupervised Denoising Pre-training Framework (DPF) for crystal structures to overcome the scarcity of labeled data in crystal property prediction. DPF pre-trains models on 380,743 unlabeled crystal structures by reconstructing masked atom types, perturbed atom positions, and perturbed lattice constants; then fine-tunes the pre-trained models on downstream crystal property prediction tasks.

task.objective: Predicting the property of a given crystal structure C = {A, P, L} by learning a function f to predict its corresponding property.
constraints: labeled data is notably scarce and varies across different properties
input_requirements: crystal structure C = {B, L} characterized by basis B = {A, P} (atom types A and positions P) and Bravais lattice L
output_goal: predicted property value (e.g., in eV/atom, eV, log(GPa))

evidence.text: The crystal property prediction problem involves predicting the property of a given crystal structure C = {A, P, L} by learning a function f to predict its corresponding property.

stages.stage_goal: Collect a large-scale dataset of unlabeled crystal structures for pre-training.

evidence.text: We pre-train our model on 380,743 crystal structure data filtered from the recent work (Merchant et al. 2023), excluding structures that are duplicates of downstream datasets or do not have physical or chemical significance.

stages.stage_goal: Generate perturbed versions of crystal structures by masking atom types, adding noise to atom positions, and perturbing lattice constants.
stage_output: perturbed crystal representations: masked atom types, perturbed atom positions, perturbed lattice constants

evidence.text: At the pre-training stage, we mask the types of crystal atoms and add noise on atom positions and lattice constants to acquire perturbed representations.

For mask language modeling, we randomly select γ of atoms in a crystal and assign a type unknown to them... For each atom in a crystal, we randomly sample a noise η ∈R3 ∼N(0, 1) and apply it to the atom positions... We also perturb the lattice constants with a randomly sampled Gaussian noise σ ∈R6 ∼N(0, 1)

stages.stage_goal: Train a model to reconstruct the original crystal structure from perturbed representations.
stage_output: pre-trained model with learned latent representation of crystal structures

evidence.text: Then perturbed crystal structures are fed into the crystal model that you want to pre-train, to reconstruct the original structure.
With the three denoising self-supervised tasks, the model is pre-trained to capture the intrinsic features of crystal structure representations.

stages.stage_goal: Adapt the pre-trained model to specific crystal property prediction tasks using labeled data.
stage_input: labeled crystal property datasets (JARVIS, Materials Project)
stage_output: fine-tuned model for downstream property prediction

evidence.text: We pre-train models on a dataset of 380,743 unlabeled crystal structures and fine-tune them on downstream property prediction tasks.
Subsequently, we fine-tune our model on downstream crystal property prediction tasks for 500 epochs

stages.stage_goal: Quantify model performance on crystal property prediction using Mean Absolute Error (MAE).
stage_input: labeled test sets from JARVIS and Materials Project
stage_output: MAE scores per property (e.g., formation energy, band gap)

evidence.text: We employ the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) to evaluate the accuracy of crystal property prediction.
